guard: manager goal-result reads canonical facts for the full authenticated caller and replies only on its derived rail
why: A real Manager spawns a harmless child and commits the terminal. Generic describe/invoke callers fetch the actual registered contract.
The owner-confusion mutant leaves the positive own-result read working but discloses it to a separately authenticated owner with the same actor and lifecycle.
The missing-reader mutant must fail the real canonical-result cell while still completing the suite, not crash in the test parser.
The open-input mutant tests the fetched closed contract. It is not claimed as a raw-wire server-validator test.
The reply-destination mutant rebuilds the actual core serveEndpoint path. A valid other caller reply rail is used, so broker destination denial cannot hide the defect.

mutations.name: M1 substitute local owner for authenticated caller owner
mutations.find: const result = await readGoalResult(gw.ctx, goalRefOf(ctx.subject, goalId));
mutations.replace: const result = await readGoalResult(gw.ctx, goalRefOf({ ...ctx.subject, caller: { ...ctx.subject.caller, owner: DEV_OWNER } }, goalId));
mutations.expectRed: goal-result does not disclose a terminal to another owner
mutations.cell: goal-result does not disclose a terminal to another owner
